results.title: La Vie a L'envers = Life Upside Down
results.brief_description:
An ordinary young Paris office worker suddenly decides to retreat into his own inner world, giving up his loquacious new wife, his friends, work and possessions. He ends up contentedly staring at a blank wall in the bare room of mental clinic. The theme of alienation, a prevalent one in the 1960s, has seldom been explored with such wry wit and sensitivity, although the film’s attitude to its hero remains ambiguous. Awards: Cannes Festival (1964): Critics’ Week Prize ; Venice Film Festival (1964): Prize for the First Work. Reference: Bloomsbury Foreign Film Guide.

Credits: Director, Alain Jessua ; writer, Alain Jessua ; photography, Jacques Robin ; music, Jacques Loussier.
Cast: Charles Denner, Anna Gaylor, Jean Yanne, Yvonne Clech, Robert Bousquet, Nicole Gueden, Guy Saint-Jean, Francois Moncey, Jean Dewewer.

results.title: Bartleby
results.brief_description:
An adaptation of Herman Melville’s story about Bartleby, the scrivener, who answers an advertisement for work with a lawyer and after a brief spurt of intense work, gradually breaks down, refuses to move, and eventually dies because he has lost the will to live.

Credits: Director, Maurice Ronet ; writers, Yvan Bostel, Maurice Ronet, Jacques Quoirez ; photography, Claude Robin ; music, Gerard Anfosso.
Cast: Michel Lonsdale, Maxence Mailfort, Maurice Biraud, Dominique Zardi, Jacques Fontanelle.

results.title: Codine
results.brief_description:
Codine has just finished a ten year sentence for murder and heads back to a Bucharest slum to be reunited with his mother, whose penny-pinching ways infuriate her son. Adrien, a young boy, befriends Codine and through his eyes discovers social injustice and the world of adults. Awards: Cannes Film Festival 1963: Best screenplay for Henri Colpi, Yves Jamiaque and Dimitriu Carabat.

Credits: Producer, Emile Breysse ; director, Henri Colpi ; writers, Henri Colpi, Yves Jamiaque, Dimitriu Carabat ; photography, Marcel Weiss ; music, Theodor Grigoriu.
Cast: Alexandru Platon, Nelly Borgeaud, Razvan Petresco, Francoise Brion, Maurice Sarfati, Nelly Borgeaud.

results.title: Amore
results.brief_description:
Michel, a young architect is sent by the French government to Venice with a mision to try and find a solution to save an island. Paolo, a young photographer, offers to help Michel in his discovery of the city. He also introduces him to the beautiful Marina.

Credits: Director, Henry Chapier ; writers, Anne Capelle, Henry Chapier ; photoraphy, Alain Derobe ; music, Vangelis Papathanassiou.
Cast: Sonia Petrova, Daniel Quenaud, Julian Negulesco, Henri Deus, Daniel Ceccaldi.

results.title: Cherchez L'idole = Look for the Idol
results.brief_description:
A young man is pushed into a dare by a girlfriend and has to steal a piece of jewellery. Interrupted in the act by nosy neighbors, he must abandon the gems in a guitar at a music shop. When he returns later to get hold of the jewels, the guitar has been sold. Musical performances by the ‘pop idols’ of the era: Charles Aznavour, Nancy Holloway, Johnny Hallyday, Sylvie Vartan and Frank Alamo.

Credits: Producer, Mario Chabert ; director, Michel Boisrond ; writers, Annette Wademant, Michel Balducci ; photography, Raymond Lemoigne ; music, Georges Garvarentz.
Cast: Frank Fernandel, Berthe Granval, Dany Saval, Mylene Demongeot, Johnny Halliday.

results.title: George Qui? = George Who?
results.brief_description:
George who? George Sand (nee Amantine-Aurore-Lucile Dupin), the renown 19th century writer who defied conventions by adopting a man’s name, garb and making her own a freedom of behavior that was strictly reserved to men. Produced in the heydays of the Women’s Movement this film depicts her life and shows she can be considered an essential forerunner of the feminist movement.

Credits: Producer, Jean-Pierre Bamberger ; director, Michele Rosier ; writer, Michele Rosier ; photography, Armand Marco.
Cast: Anne Wiazemsky, Jean-Gabriel Nordmann.

results.title: Dis-Moi Que Tu M'aimes = Tell Me You Love Me
results.creator_credit: Michel Boisrond, Francis Cosne and Gerard Beytout
results.brief_description:
Bertrand and Richard both work in an advertising agency. Richard is married to sweet and submissive Charlotte, whom he treats harshly. Victoire, Bertrand’s wife is less than impressed by this display of chauvinism. Both couple decide to experiment with temporary separation. The men setup camp at the office and the women share a house.

Credits: Producers, Gerard Beytout, Francis Cosne ; director, Michel Boisrond ; writers, Michel Boisrond, Annette Wademant ; photography, Daniel Gaudry ; music, Claude Bolling.
Cast: Mireille Darc, Daniel Ceccaldi, Marie-Jose Nat, Jean-Pierre Marielle, Jean-Pierre Darras.

results.title: Le Petit Marcel = Little Marcel
results.brief_description:
After he inherits his father’s truck, Marcel makes the big trip to Paris in the hope of setting up a transport business. While awaiting the his truck rego, he becomes involved with a gang of people under police surveillance.

Credits: Director, Jacques Fansten ; writers, Jean-Claude Grumberg, Jacques Fansten ; photography, Jean Gonnet ; music, Graeme Allwright.
Cast: Jacques Spiesser, Isabelle Huppert, Yves Robert, Jean-Francois Balmer, Michel Aumont, Anouk Ferjak ; Hubert Gignoux.

results.title: Les Aventures de Salavin = the Adventures of Salavin
results.brief_description:
The Salavin cycle describes the frustrations and perplexities of a ‘little man’ of the 20th century trying to work out his own salvation with no religious faith to sustain him.

Credits: Producer, Edgar Roulleau ; director, Pierre Granier-Deferre ; writers, Pierre Granier-Deferre, R. M. Arland ; photography, Rene Bucaille ; music, Claude Bolling.
Cast: Maurice Biraud, Christiane Minazzoli, Mona Dol, Genevieve Fontanel, Julien Carette.

results.title: Leonor = Expulsion of the Devil
results.brief_description:
During the middle-ages, Lord Richard is away at the war when he learns of the death of his wife, Leonor. Stricken with grief, he burries her in the crypt of his castle and re-marries that same night with a young girl, Catherine. Thanks to Catherine and their two children, Richard is re-born, but still has difficulties forgetting his first wife. He decides to re-open the crypt and live there with Leonor, in spite of a warning from an old man that reviving the dead can be an extremely hazardous activity. Soon after, Leonor comes out of the crypt to resume life with Richard and asks him to kill Catherine and the children.

Credits: Director, Juan Bunuel ; writers, Jean-Claude Carriere ; Juan Bunuel, Michel Nuritzani, Pierre Maintigneux ; photography, Luciano Tovoli ; music, Ennio Morricone.
Cast: Liv Ullman, Michel Piccoli, Ornella Mutti, Antonio Ferrandis.
